tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to read

offset.description: The line number to start reading from. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once

limit.description: The number of lines to read. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once.

pages.description: Page range for PDF files (e.g., "1-5", "3", "10-20"). Only applicable to PDF files. Maximum 20 pages per request.

allow_large.description: Set to true to read a text file, or a line range of one, that is over the usual size limits, up to what still fits in your context. Only use this when you genuinely need all of it or the user asked for the whole file; otherwise read it in parts with offset and limit, or search it.

tools.name: ReportFindings
tools.description: Report code-review findings as a typed list so the host UI can render them. Use this only when the active code-review instructions tell you to report findings with this tool; otherwise follow whatever output format those instructions specify. When reporting a review's results, call it once with the verified findings ranked most-severe first (empty array if nothing survived verification) and do not also print the findings as text. When re-reporting after applying fixes (only if the apply instructions ask for it), set `outcome` on each finding to what actually happened.

level.description: Effort level the review ran at

findings.description: Verified findings, most-severe first; empty if none survived

file.description: Repo-relative path of the file the finding is in

short_summary.description: Compressed label for compact UI (≤60 chars): the claim alone, no rationale or consequence clause

category.description: Short kebab-case slug of the finding type, e.g. "correctness", "simplification", "efficiency", "test-coverage"

verdict.description: Set when a verify pass ran; absent on inline-only reviews

outcome.description: Set ONLY when re-reporting after applying fixes: what happened to this finding

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

delaySeconds.description: Seconds from now to wake up. Clamped to [60, 3600] by the runtime. Required unless `stop` is true.

reason.description: One short sentence explaining the chosen delay. Goes to telemetry and is shown to the user. Be specific. Required unless `stop` is true.

prompt.description: The /loop input to fire on wake-up. Pass the same /loop input verbatim each turn so the next firing re-enters the skill and continues the loop. For autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` instead (the dynamic-pacing variant, not the CronCreate-mode `<<autonomous-loop>>`). Required unless `stop` is true.

stop.description: Set to true to end the dynamic loop immediately instead of scheduling another wakeup. When true, all other fields are ignored and no further wakeups fire.

noop.description: true = nothing changed (you checked and there is nothing to report). false = something happened worth keeping (edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, surfaced a finding). Consecutive noop:true ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak. Required unless `stop` is true.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

skill.description: The name of a skill from the available-skills list. Do not guess names.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

query.description: Query to find deferred tools. Use "select:<tool_name>" for direct selection, or keywords to search.

max_results.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 5)

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with the same `scriptPath` instead of re-sending the full script. Takes precedence over `script` and `name`.

resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. Completed agent() calls with unchanged (prompt, opts) return their cached results instantly; only edited or new calls re-run. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

tools.name: mcp__plugin_context-mode_context-mode__ctx_fetch_and_index
tools.description:
Fetches URL content, converts HTML to markdown (JSON is chunked by key paths, plain text indexed directly), persists it in a searchable knowledge base, and returns a small preview window per source. The raw page bytes never enter your conversation — they live in storage and you retrieve any section on-demand via ctx_search.

Caching: every fetch is cached on disk and reused for repeat calls within the TTL window. The default TTL is 24 hours; override per-call with the `ttl` parameter (milliseconds, `ttl: 0` bypasses cache like `force: true`). Stored content older than 14 days is cleaned up on startup.

WHEN:
  - You need web content (docs, changelogs, API references, spec pages) and the raw page bytes should NOT enter your conversation
  - Multi-URL research (library evaluation, migration scans, doc comparisons): pass the `requests` array and a `concurrency` value 2-8 for parallel I/O
  - You want repeat lookups against the same URL to be cheap (TTL cache hits return only a hint, no re-fetch)
  - You want a long-lived cache window (override `ttl` upward for stable specs) or a guaranteed-fresh fetch (`ttl: 0` or `force: true`)

WHEN NOT:
  - You already have the content locally — store it via the inline index tool
  - The page is SPA-rendered (JavaScript-required to materialize content) — this is a plain HTTP fetch, no headless browser

RETURNS:
  Per-source preview windows extracted around indexable headings plus indexing metadata (chunk counts, source labels, cache state). Raw content is NOT echoed back — retrieve any section on-demand via ctx_search(source: "<label>"). Concurrency parallelizes the fetch phase up to your chosen value (capped by the host's logical CPU count); the FTS5 write phase always runs serially because SQLite is a single-writer store. Net latency = max(fetch latency across the pool) + sum(per-source index write time). Cache hits skip both phases and return a small freshness hint instead of re-fetching. Use 4-8 for stable I/O-bound batches; lower the value when the target host enforces a per-IP rate limit you cannot raise.

EXAMPLE: ctx_fetch_and_index(
  requests: [{url: "https://react.dev/...", source: "react"}, {url: "https://vuejs.org/...", source: "vue"}],
  concurrency: 5
)

url.description: Single URL to fetch and index (legacy single-shape)

source.description: Label for the indexed content when using single `url` (e.g., 'React useEffect docs', 'Supabase Auth API'). For batch, put source in each requests entry.
Label for this URL's indexed content

requests.description: Batch shape: array of {url, source?} entries. Use with concurrency>1 for parallel fetch. Each request indexed under its own source label. Output preserves input order.

concurrency.description: Max URLs to fetch in parallel (1-8, default: 1). Use 4-8 for I/O-bound multi-URL batches (library docs, changelogs, pricing pages). Capped by os.cpus().length on small machines (response notes when capped). Indexing is always serial regardless — only fetches race.

force.description: Skip cache and re-fetch even if content was recently indexed

ttl.description: Override the cache freshness window for this call, in milliseconds. `ttl: 0` bypasses the cache like `force: true`; omit to use the default 24h TTL.

tools.name: mcp__plugin_context-mode_context-mode__ctx_search
tools.description:
Search a unified knowledge base with a multi-strategy ranking pipeline. Two parallel matchers run on every query: a Porter-stemming matcher ("caching" finds "cached", "caches", "cach") and a trigram-substring matcher ("useEff" finds "useEffect"). Their ranked lists are merged via Reciprocal Rank Fusion, so a document that ranks well in both surfaces above one that wins only on a single strategy. Multi-term queries get an additional proximity-rerank pass that boosts passages where the query terms appear close together. Typos are corrected via Levenshtein distance and re-searched. Result snippets are window-extracted around the matched terms, not blindly truncated.

The knowledge base is unified: queries reach indexed content you stored (ctx_index, ctx_fetch_and_index, ctx_batch_execute output) AND auto-captured session memory written by hooks (decisions, errors, blockers, plans, user prompts, rejected approaches, tool failures, compaction guides — 26 event categories). File-backed sources carry a content hash and auto-flag staleness when the source file changes.

WHEN:
  - You want to recall something that exists in storage (recently indexed content, prior session events, auto-memory) instead of re-reading raw sources
  - You have multiple related questions about the same body of knowledge — batch every question into one call (the ranking pipeline runs per-query but the round-trip cost is paid once)
  - You want to scope the query to one labelled source (pass `source` — partial match is fine)
  - You want a chronological view across current session + prior sessions + persistent auto-memory (pass `sort: "timeline"` — the default `relevance` mode only ranks within the current session)
  - You want to filter ranked results by content shape (pass `contentType: "code"` to surface implementation snippets or `contentType: "prose"` to surface explanations)

WHEN NOT:
  - The data you want to query has never been stored in the knowledge base AND no session memory has accumulated around it — capture first (run a gather-and-index call), then come back here to query
  - You have one ad-hoc question against data that is not in the knowledge base — answer it inline by running code in the sandbox tool; one round-trip instead of capture-then-query

RETURNS:
  Per-query ranked sections with window-extracted snippets. Use 2-4 specific technical terms per query. Common session-memory source labels: `decision` (user corrections / preferences), `error` and `error-resolution` (past failures + their fixes), `blocker`, `plan`, `user-prompt`, `rejected-approach`, `compaction` (post-compact session guide). See ctx_stats for live category counts.

EXAMPLE: ctx_search(queries: ["root cause", "proposed fix", "test coverage"], source: "issue-#683")
EXAMPLE: ctx_search(queries: ["what did we decide about caching"], source: "decision", sort: "timeline")
EXAMPLE: ctx_search(queries: ["useEffect cleanup pattern"], source: "react-docs", contentType: "code", limit: 5)
EXAMPLE: ctx_search(queries: ["last user prompt", "active skills", "open blockers"], sort: "timeline")

queries.description: Array of search queries. Batch ALL questions in one call.

source.description: Filter to a specific indexed source (partial match).

contentType.description: Filter results by content type: 'code' or 'prose'.

sort.description: Sort mode. 'relevance' (default): BM25 ranked, current session only. 'timeline': chronological across current session, prior sessions, and auto-memory.

content.text: Tool loaded.

lastPrompt: re-record the baseline. We should move towards the CodeScene scores as much as possible. Continue the iteration

406	    """

409	    config: LayerConfig = load_config(archy_yaml_path)
410	    layer_modules = {layer.name: list(layer.patterns) for layer in config.layers}

def governed_roots(config: LayerConfig) -> frozenset[str]:
    """The top-level packages the config's LAYER PATTERNS talk about.

    A pattern is a dotted-name glob whose first segment names the namespace the
    author intended to govern, except a floating one (`**.services.**`), which
    names no namespace. Any floating pattern makes the scope unbounded, so this
    returns the empty set and `compute_coverage` does not scope by root.

    NOT `LayerConfig.roots`, despite the name proximity. That field declares
    extra PEP 420 scan roots so the graph builder can find namespace packages at
    all; this function asks which namespaces the rules claim authority over.
    Neither reads the other.
    """
    patterns = [pattern for layer in config.layers for pattern in layer.patterns]
    if any(is_floating_pattern(pattern) for pattern in patterns):
        return frozenset()
    return frozenset(pattern.split(".")[0] for pattern in patterns)


def compute_coverage(graph: nx.DiGraph, config: LayerConfig) -> LayerCoverage:
    """Measure the reach of `config`'s layers over `graph`.

    Scoped to the root packages the config names, NOT to everything the scan
    happened to reach. `archy check .` on this repository walks `bench/` too,
    and counting those scripts would report 7% coverage for a config that never
    claimed to govern them. The interpretable question is "of the code you said
    you were governing, how much do the rules reach", and modules outside those
    roots are counted separately rather than silently dropped.

    External nodes are not the user's code, so they stay out of the module and
    internal-edge counts. A layer that NAMES an external package
    (`sqlalchemy.**`) is still a layer that exists: the external nodes it
    matches count toward `layer_sizes` (so presence is true), and the edges into
    them are reported apart as `external_edges_governed` (#527).
    """
    ruled_layers = {rule.from_layer for rule in config.forbid} | {
        rule.to_layer for rule in config.forbid
    }
    roots = governed_roots(config)
    layer_of: dict[str, str | None] = {}
    external_layer_of: dict[str, str] = {}
    outside = 0
    for node, data in graph.nodes(data=True):
        if data.get("external"):
            external_layer = match_layer(node, config.layers)
            if external_layer is not None:
                external_layer_of[node] = external_layer
            continue
        if roots and node.split(".")[0] not in roots:
            outside += 1
            continue
        layer_of[node] = match_layer(node, config.layers)

    sizes = {layer.name: 0 for layer in config.layers}
    for layer in (*layer_of.values(), *external_layer_of.values()):
        if layer is not None:
            sizes[layer] = sizes.get(layer, 0) + 1

    matched = [node for node, layer in layer_of.items() if layer is not None]
    in_ruled = [node for node, layer in layer_of.items() if layer in ruled_layers]
    unlayered = sorted(node for node, layer in layer_of.items() if layer is None)

    internal_edges = [(src, dst) for src, dst in graph.edges if src in layer_of and dst in layer_of]
    governed = [
        (src, dst)
        for src, dst in internal_edges
        if layer_of[src] is not None and layer_of[dst] is not None
    ]

    external_governed = sum(
        1 for src, dst in graph.edges if layer_of.get(src) is not None and dst in external_layer_of
    )

    return LayerCoverage(
        exact_pattern_hints=_exact_pattern_hints(config, unlayered),
        external_edges_governed=external_governed,
        modules_total=len(layer_of),
        modules_matched=len(matched),
        modules_in_ruled_layer=len(in_ruled),
        edges_total=len(internal_edges),
        edges_governed=len(governed),
        unlayered_modules=tuple(unlayered),
        modules_outside_declared_roots=outside,
        layer_sizes=tuple((layer.name, sizes[layer.name]) for layer in config.layers),
    )

    config: LayerConfig, coverage: LayerCoverage, violations: list[Violation]
) -> bool:

def match_layer(qualname: str, layers: tuple[LayerSpec, ...]) -> str | None:
    """Return the layer name covering `qualname`, or None if unlayered.

    Layers are expected to be disjoint. That is checked here at runtime (the
    walk collects all matches and raises if a module matches more than one),
    not at load_config, which validates pattern *syntax* but not cross-layer
    overlap. Disjointness can only be decided against a concrete module set.
    """
    matches = [layer.name for layer in layers if _qualname_matches_any(qualname, layer.patterns)]
    if len(matches) > 1:
        raise LayerConfigError(
            f"module {qualname!r} matches multiple layers ({', '.join(matches)}); "
            "make pattern coverage disjoint"
        )
    return matches[0] if matches else None


def check_external_patterns(graph: nx.DiGraph, config: LayerConfig) -> None:
    """Refuse a pattern that reaches below an external package's top-level name.

    The graph collapses every external import to its top-level package, so
    `from sqlalchemy.orm import Session` is an edge to the node `sqlalchemy` and
    there is never a node `sqlalchemy.orm`. A pattern such as `sqlalchemy.orm.**`
    can therefore never match, and `check` exited 0 on a real import it was
    written to catch (#527). Decided against the graph, not at YAML load: only
    a scanned tree says which first segments are external packages and which are
    the project's own.

    Raises:
        LayerConfigError: naming the pattern and the form that works.
    """
    external = {n for n, d in graph.nodes(data=True) if d.get("external")}
    if not external:
        return
    named: list[tuple[str, str]] = []
    for layer in config.layers:
        named.extend((f"layer {layer.name!r}", pattern) for pattern in layer.patterns)
    for rule in config.required:
        for field, pattern in (
            ("source", rule.source),
            ("must_reach", rule.must_reach),
            ("within", rule.within),
        ):
            if pattern and pattern != ENTRYPOINTS_SOURCE:
                named.append((f"required rule {field}", pattern))
    for where, pattern in named:
        if is_floating_pattern(pattern):
            continue
        root = pattern.split(".", 1)[0]
        if root in external and pattern not in (root, f"{root}.**"):
            raise LayerConfigError(
                f"{where} pattern {pattern!r} names a submodule of the external package "
                f"{root!r}, but the graph keeps only the top-level name, so it can never "
                f"match. Use {root + '.**'!r}."
            )


def find_violations(graph: nx.DiGraph, config: LayerConfig) -> list[Violation]:
    check_external_patterns(graph, config)
    forbid_index = {(rule.from_layer, rule.to_layer): rule for rule in config.forbid}
    violations: list[Violation] = []
    for source, target, data in graph.edges(data=True):
        src_layer = match_layer(source, config.layers)
        tgt_layer = match_layer(target, config.layers)
        if src_layer is None or tgt_layer is None:
            continue
        rule = forbid_index.get((src_layer, tgt_layer))
        if rule is None:
            continue
        violations.append(
            Violation(
                rule=rule,
                source=source,
                target=target,
                lines=tuple(data.get("lines", ())),
                path=graph.graph.get("relative_paths", {}).get(source, ""),
            )
        )
    violations.sort(key=lambda v: (v.rule.from_layer, v.rule.to_layer, v.source, v.target))
    return violations


def find_reach_violations(graph: nx.DiGraph, config: LayerConfig) -> list[ReachViolation]:
    """Every `required:` rule that a module fails to satisfy.

    Reach is transitive and computed over `graph.with_package_init_edges`, so a
    package that imports the target once in its `__init__.py` satisfies the rule
    for all of its submodules. A module trivially satisfies a rule it matches on
    both sides (it reaches itself).

    Rules that cannot fire are reported here too, as violations with
    `module=None`. Skipping them would reproduce the failure that motivated
    layer coverage: a typo'd pattern matching nothing looks exactly like a
    codebase that satisfies the rule everywhere.

    Cost is one `nx.descendants` per matching source module. Fine for the shapes
    this targets (a `commands.**` package, a handful of entrypoints); a rule
    whose `source` is a bare `**`-rooted pattern over a very large tree pays for
    the breadth it asked for.
    """
    if not config.required:
        return []
    check_external_patterns(graph, config)

    # `archy.reach`, NOT `archy.graph`, which is where this helper first lived.
    # graph pulls in parser/complexity/risk behind it, so importing it here put
    # policy 4 hops from a leaf and cost 2 on max import depth. Both spellings
    # pass `archy check` (policy -> graph is permitted) and both type-check; the
    # depth axis is what caught it, and archy's own `LayerConfig.max_modules`
    # comment already recorded the intent that policy not depend on graph.
    # A function-local import would NOT have helped: archy records function-local
    # imports as graph edges (tests/test_graph.py pins that), so the edge and the
    # depth cost are identical either way.
    from archy.reach import with_package_init_edges

    augmented = with_package_init_edges(graph)
    all_nodes = list(graph.nodes)
    internal = [n for n, d in graph.nodes(data=True) if not d.get("external")]

    violations: list[ReachViolation] = []
    for rule in config.required:
        # Targets may be external: "every entrypoint must reach `sqlalchemy`" is
        # a legitimate thing to require, and external nodes are real nodes here.
        targets = {n for n in all_nodes if _qualname_matches_any(n, (rule.must_reach,))}
        why: dict[str, str] = {}
        if rule.source == ENTRYPOINTS_SOURCE:
            errors = graph.graph.get("entrypoint_errors", ())
            if errors:
                # The derived set is incomplete, so a pass would be a pass over
                # a subset nobody chose. Refuse the verdict rather than give it.
                violations.append(
                    ReachViolation(
                        rule=rule,
                        module=None,
                        detail=f"entrypoints could not be fully derived: {'; '.join(errors)}",
                    )
                )
                continue
            derived = graph.graph.get("entrypoints", {})
            why = {
                n: reason
                for n, reason in derived.items()
                if rule.within is None or _qualname_matches_any(n, (rule.within,))
            }
            sources = sorted(n for n in internal if n in why)
        else:
            sources = sorted(n for n in internal if _qualname_matches_any(n, (rule.source,)))
        if not targets:
            violations.append(
                ReachViolation(
                    rule=rule,
                    module=None,
                    detail=(
                        f"nothing matches the `must_reach` pattern {rule.must_reach!r} in the "
                        "scanned tree: either the pattern is wrong, or -- for an external "
                        "package -- no module imports it any more, which is itself the "
                        "failure the rule is about."
                    ),
                )
            )
            continue
        if not sources and rule.source == ENTRYPOINTS_SOURCE:
            scope = "" if rule.within is None else f" within {rule.within!r}"
            violations.append(
                ReachViolation(
                    rule=rule,
                    module=None,
                    detail=(
                        f"rule cannot fire: no entrypoint was derived{scope}. An entrypoint is a "
                        'module with a top-level `if __name__ == "__main__":` guard, a '
                        "`__main__.py`, or a script target in a pyproject.toml between the "
                        "scanned modules and the repository root."
                    ),
                )
            )
            continue
        if not sources:
            violations.append(
                ReachViolation(
                    rule=rule,
                    module=None,
                    detail=(
                        f"rule cannot fire: `source` pattern {rule.source!r} matches no internal "
                        'module (patterns are dotted-name globs -- "pkg.**" matches a package and '
                        'its descendants, "pkg" only that exact module).'
                    ),
                )
            )
            continue
        for module in sources:
            if module in targets:
                continue
            if nx.descendants(augmented, module) & targets:
                continue
            violations.append(
                ReachViolation(
                    rule=rule,
                    module=module,
                    detail=(
                        f"{module} does not transitively reach {rule.must_reach!r} "
                        "(package __init__ imports included)."
                        + (f" It is an entrypoint: {why[module]}." if module in why else "")
                    ),
                )
            )
    violations.sort(
        key=lambda v: (v.rule.source, v.rule.within or "", v.rule.must_reach, v.module or "")
    )
    return violations


def find_sdp_violations(graph: nx.DiGraph, *, tolerance: float = 0.0) -> list[SdpViolation]:
    """Edges where the target is strictly less stable than the source.

    "Less stable" means higher Martin's I. The Stable Dependencies
    Principle says modules should depend in the direction of stability,
    so an edge from `Is = 0.2` to `It = 0.8` (target depends on more
    things, more likely to change) is a violation. Only internal-to-
    internal edges are considered; external dependencies have no I.
    """
    instability = compute_instability(graph)
    violations: list[SdpViolation] = []
    for source, target, data in graph.edges(data=True):
        if source not in instability or target not in instability:
            continue
        i_src = instability[source]
        i_tgt = instability[target]
        if i_tgt > i_src + tolerance:
            violations.append(
                SdpViolation(
                    source=source,
                    target=target,
                    source_instability=i_src,
                    target_instability=i_tgt,
                    lines=tuple(data.get("lines", ())),
                    path=graph.graph.get("relative_paths", {}).get(source, ""),
                )
            )
    violations.sort(key=lambda v: (v.source, v.target))
    return violations

376	def governed_roots(config: LayerConfig) -> frozenset[str]:
377	    """The top-level packages the config's LAYER PATTERNS talk about.
378	
379	    A pattern is a dotted-name glob whose first segment names the namespace the
380	    author intended to govern, except a floating one (`**.services.**`), which
381	    names no namespace. Any floating pattern makes the scope unbounded, so this
382	    returns the empty set and `compute_coverage` does not scope by root.
383	
384	    NOT `LayerConfig.roots`, despite the name proximity. That field declares
385	    extra PEP 420 scan roots so the graph builder can find namespace packages at
386	    all; this function asks which namespaces the rules claim authority over.
387	    Neither reads the other.
388	    """
389	    patterns = [pattern for layer in config.layers for pattern in layer.patterns]
390	    if any(is_floating_pattern(pattern) for pattern in patterns):
391	        return frozenset()
392	    return frozenset(pattern.split(".")[0] for pattern in patterns)

395	def compute_coverage(graph: nx.DiGraph, config: LayerConfig) -> LayerCoverage:
396	    """Measure the reach of `config`'s layers over `graph`.
397	
398	    Scoped to the root packages the config names, NOT to everything the scan
399	    happened to reach. `archy check .` on this repository walks `bench/` too,
400	    and counting those scripts would report 7% coverage for a config that never
401	    claimed to govern them. The interpretable question is "of the code you said
402	    you were governing, how much do the rules reach", and modules outside those
403	    roots are counted separately rather than silently dropped.
404	
405	    External nodes are not the user's code, so they stay out of the module and
406	    internal-edge counts. A layer that NAMES an external package
407	    (`sqlalchemy.**`) is still a layer that exists: the external nodes it
408	    matches count toward `layer_sizes` (so presence is true), and the edges into
409	    them are reported apart as `external_edges_governed` (#527).
410	    """
411	    ruled_layers = {rule.from_layer for rule in config.forbid} | {
412	        rule.to_layer for rule in config.forbid
413	    }
414	    roots = governed_roots(config)
415	    layer_of: dict[str, str | None] = {}
416	    external_layer_of: dict[str, str] = {}
417	    outside = 0
418	    for node, data in graph.nodes(data=True):
419	        if data.get("external"):
420	            external_layer = match_layer(node, config.layers)
421	            if external_layer is not None:
422	                external_layer_of[node] = external_layer
423	            continue
424	        if roots and node.split(".")[0] not in roots:
425	            outside += 1
426	            continue
427	        layer_of[node] = match_layer(node, config.layers)
428	
429	    sizes = {layer.name: 0 for layer in config.layers}
430	    for layer in (*layer_of.values(), *external_layer_of.values()):
431	        if layer is not None:
432	            sizes[layer] = sizes.get(layer, 0) + 1
433	
434	    matched = [node for node, layer in layer_of.items() if layer is not None]
435	    in_ruled = [node for node, layer in layer_of.items() if layer in ruled_layers]
436	    unlayered = sorted(node for node, layer in layer_of.items() if layer is None)
437	
438	    internal_edges = [(src, dst) for src, dst in graph.edges if src in layer_of and dst in layer_of]
439	    governed = [
440	        (src, dst)
441	        for src, dst in internal_edges
442	        if layer_of[src] is not None and layer_of[dst] is not None
443	    ]
444	
445	    external_governed = sum(
446	        1 for src, dst in graph.edges if layer_of.get(src) is not None and dst in external_layer_of
447	    )
448	
449	    return LayerCoverage(
450	        exact_pattern_hints=_exact_pattern_hints(config, unlayered),

700	    walk collects all matches and raises if a module matches more than one),

702	    overlap. Disjointness can only be decided against a concrete module set.
703	    """

713	def check_external_patterns(graph: nx.DiGraph, config: LayerConfig) -> None:
714	    """Refuse a pattern that reaches below an external package's top-level name.
715

717	    `from sqlalchemy.orm import Session` is an edge to the node `sqlalchemy` and
718	    there is never a node `sqlalchemy.orm`. A pattern such as `sqlalchemy.orm.**`
719	    can therefore never match, and `check` exited 0 on a real import it was
720	    written to catch (#527). Decided against the graph, not at YAML load: only
721	    a scanned tree says which first segments are external packages and which are
722	    the project's own.
723	
724	    Raises:
725	        LayerConfigError: naming the pattern and the form that works.
726	    """
727	    external = {n for n, d in graph.nodes(data=True) if d.get("external")}
728	    if not external:
729	        return
730	    named: list[tuple[str, str]] = []
731	    for layer in config.layers:
732	        named.extend((f"layer {layer.name!r}", pattern) for pattern in layer.patterns)
733	    for rule in config.required:
734	        for field, pattern in (

753	def find_violations(graph: nx.DiGraph, config: LayerConfig) -> list[Violation]:
754	    check_external_patterns(graph, config)
755	    forbid_index = {(rule.from_layer, rule.to_layer): rule for rule in config.forbid}
756	    violations: list[Violation] = []
757	    for source, target, data in graph.edges(data=True):
758	        src_layer = match_layer(source, config.layers)
759	        tgt_layer = match_layer(target, config.layers)
760	        if src_layer is None or tgt_layer is None:

772	            )

780

782	    package that imports the target once in its `__init__.py` satisfies the rule
783	    for all of its submodules. A module trivially satisfies a rule it matches on
784	    both sides (it reaches itself).

787	    `module=None`. Skipping them would reproduce the failure that motivated

832	                )

835	            why = {

838	                if rule.within is None or _qualname_matches_any(n, (rule.within,))
839	            }
840	            sources = sorted(n for n in internal if n in why)
841	        else:

850	                        "scanned tree: either the pattern is wrong, or -- for an external "
851	                        "package -- no module imports it any more, which is itself the "
852	                        "failure the rule is about."
853	                    ),
854	                )
855	            )
856	            continue

858	            scope = "" if rule.within is None else f" within {rule.within!r}"
859	            violations.append(
860	                ReachViolation(
861	                    rule=rule,
862	                    module=None,
863	                    detail=(
864	                        f"rule cannot fire: no entrypoint was derived{scope}. An entrypoint is a "
865	                        'module with a top-level `if __name__ == "__main__":` guard, a '
866	                        "`__main__.py`, or a script target in a pyproject.toml between the "
867	                        "scanned modules and the repository root."
868	                    ),

879	                        'module (patterns are dotted-name globs -- "pkg.**" matches a package and '
880	                        'its descendants, "pkg" only that exact module).'
881	                    ),

896	                        "(package __init__ imports included)."

907	def find_sdp_violations(graph: nx.DiGraph, *, tolerance: float = 0.0) -> list[SdpViolation]:
908	    """Edges where the target is strictly less stable than the source.
909	
910	    "Less stable" means higher Martin's I. The Stable Dependencies
911	    Principle says modules should depend in the direction of stability,
912	    so an edge from `Is = 0.2` to `It = 0.8` (target depends on more
913	    things, more likely to change) is a violation. Only internal-to-
914	    internal edges are considered; external dependencies have no I.
915	    """
916	    instability = compute_instability(graph)
917	    violations: list[SdpViolation] = []
918	    for source, target, data in graph.edges(data=True):
919	        if source not in instability or target not in instability:
920	            continue
921	        i_src = instability[source]
922	        i_tgt = instability[target]
923	        if i_tgt > i_src + tolerance:
924	            violations.append(
925	                SdpViolation(
926	                    source=source,
927	                    target=target,
928	                    source_instability=i_src,
929	                    target_instability=i_tgt,
930	                    lines=tuple(data.get("lines", ())),
931	                    path=graph.graph.get("relative_paths", {}).get(source, ""),
932	                )
933	            )
934	    violations.sort(key=lambda v: (v.source, v.target))

def _reach_graph(*edges: tuple[str, str], nodes: tuple[str, ...] = ()) -> nx.DiGraph:
    """A graph whose nodes carry the `external=False` marker real scans set."""
    g: nx.DiGraph = nx.DiGraph()
    for node in nodes:
        g.add_node(node, external=False)
    for u, v in edges:
        g.add_node(u, external=False)
        g.add_node(v, external=False)
        g.add_edge(u, v, lines=(1,))
    return g


_REGISTRY_CONFIG = (
    "layers: {}\nforbid: []\n"
    "required:\n"
    "  - source: 'commands.**'\n"
    "    must_reach: core.database.model_registry\n"
    "    reason: standalone entrypoints need the full mapper registry\n"
)


def test_required_reach_bootstrap_import_is_load_bearing(tmp_path: Path):
    """Negative control: the SAME graph, with only the bootstrap edge removed.

    Asked for by the incident reporter, who shipped a guard for this exact bug
    that passed with the fix REVERTED -- it asserted `configure_mappers()`
    succeeds, and with no models imported there are no mappers to configure. The
    generalizable failure is that a reach assertion over an under-connected
    graph passes vacuously, and an under-connected graph is what archy had
    before `package_init_edges`. A test that only asserts the clean case cannot
    tell "the rule is satisfied" from "the rule never fired".

    So both halves are pinned here, on one fixture, with one edge between them.
    """
    config = _cfg(tmp_path, _REGISTRY_CONFIG)
    satisfied = _reach_graph(
        ("commands", "core.database.model_registry"),
        nodes=("commands.setup_user", "commands.backfill", "core.database"),
    )

    assert find_reach_violations(satisfied, config) == []

    # Nothing else changes: drop the one import in `commands/__init__.py`.
    reverted = satisfied.copy()
    reverted.remove_edge("commands", "core.database.model_registry")

    assert [v.module for v in find_reach_violations(reverted, config)] == [
        "commands",
        "commands.backfill",
        "commands.setup_user",
    ]
    import of the registry.
    """
    config = _cfg(tmp_path, _REGISTRY_CONFIG)
    graph = _reach_graph(
        ("commands", "core.database.model_registry"),
        nodes=("commands.orphan",),
    )

    assert find_reach_violations(graph, config) == []

import json, re, subprocess, sys
from pathlib import Path
sys.path.insert(0, sys.argv[1]); import split_cli_groups as G
owner = {n: m for m, names in G.GROUPS.items() for n in names}
mods = list(G.GROUPS)
out = subprocess.run(["uv","run","ruff","check","--select","F821","--output-format","json"]+[f"src/archy/{m}.py" for m in mods],capture_output=True,text=True).stdout
need = {}
for d in json.loads(out):
    name = re.search(r"`(.+?)`", d["message"]).group(1)
    mod = Path(d["filename"]).stem
    if name not in owner: print("UNOWNED", mod, name); continue
    if owner[name] == mod: print("SAME-MODULE?", mod, name); continue
    need.setdefault(mod, {}).setdefault(owner[name], set()).add(name)
for mod, by_owner in need.items():
    p = Path(f"src/archy/{mod}.py"); s = p.read_text()
    block = "".join(f"from archy.{o} import {', '.join(sorted(n))}\n" for o, n in sorted(by_owner.items()))
    # insert after the last top-level 'from archy.' import line
    idx = [m.end() for m in re.finditer(r"^from archy\.[^\n]*(?:\n    [^\n]*)*\n(?:\)\n)?", s, re.M)]
    pos = idx[-1] if idx else s.index("\n\n")
    p.write_text(s[:pos] + block + s[pos:])
    print(mod, {o: sorted(n) for o, n in by_owner.items()})

CodeScene's file-level **Low Cohesion** smell ("the functions in this module serve unrelated responsibilities") flagged `layers.py` at 4.85 and was the one smell the in-place Complex Method pass (#920) could not clear. The module split in #922 cleared it. archy has no equivalent: `what-to-refactor-next` ranks by risk and churn but never says "this file should be split, and along these lines".

Proposal (advisory, no change to the score, per #886's line on not moving the score's definition):
- Build the graph of a module's top-level definitions, with an edge when one definition references another (call, base class, annotation, module constant). Connected components of that graph, after removing names every component uses (a shared exception or constant), are candidate responsibilities.
- Report a module whose definitions split into 2+ components each at or above a size floor, listing the members of each. Write this as a split plan: the grouping is the actionable output.

Falsifiable check before building: run it on the pre-split `layers.py` (kept in git history at the parent of #922) and on the pre-split `cli.py`, `conventions.py` and `cli_render.py`. If its components do not resemble the groups the splits actually used (models / matching / config / checking), the heuristic is not worth shipping. Pre-register the agreement threshold in the ticket before running.

Anti-theater: this only earns its place if the components predict where a human would cut; a module that is merely long should not be flagged, and CodeScene's own threshold (it flags on cohesion, not size) is the thing to match. Related: #872, #899, #916.
EOF

def run_duplicates(
    path: Path,
    *,
    response_format: str,
    min_nodes: int,
    top_n: int,
    members: int,
    co_change: bool = True,
    near_miss: bool = False,
) -> DuplicatesPayload:
    """Two-tier duplicate clusters for archy_duplicates.

    Reads per-function rows via the function-grained warm path (`parse_map`),
    classifies clusters into the primary/variant tiers, and shapes each tier by
    `response_format` (a per-cluster summary vs the full member lists). When
    `co_change` and git history is available, demotes primary clusters whose
    copies never co-change (issue #242); best-effort (no git -> unchanged). When
    `near_miss`, adds a lower-confidence Type-3 tier via token overlap (#246).
    """
    _validate_response_format(response_format)
    if min_nodes < 1:
        raise ValueError(f"min_nodes must be >= 1; got {min_nodes}")
    if top_n < 1:
        raise ValueError(f"top_n must be >= 1; got {top_n}")
    if members < 2:
        raise ValueError(f"members must be >= 2; got {members}")
    modules, results = _parse_project(
        path, max_modules=resolve_max_modules(path), **graph_kwargs(path)
    )
    rows = classify_variants(
        compute_duplicates(modules, results, min_size=min_nodes, min_members=members)
    )
    if co_change:
        cochange = git_cochange(path, keep_paths=frozenset(str(m.path) for m in modules))
        if cochange is not None:
            rows = demote_independent(
                rows, counts=cochange.counts, pair_support=cochange.pair_support
            )
    near = compute_near_duplicates(modules, results, min_size=min_nodes) if near_miss else []
    dups = [g for g in rows if g.category == "duplicate"]
    variants = [g for g in rows if g.category == "variant"]

    def _shape(groups: list[DuplicateGroup]):
        top = groups[:top_n]
        if response_format == "full":
            return tuple(top)
        return tuple(_summarize_duplicate_group(g) for g in top)

    note: str | None = None
    if not dups:
        note = (
            f"No likely-duplicate function bodies of >= {min_nodes} normalized "
            "nodes found; lower min_nodes to widen the search."
        )
        if variants:
            note += (
                f" ({len(variants)} likely-intentional variant(s) were found but demoted: "
                "same-class / boilerplate / test / vendored / independent.)"
            )
    return DuplicatesPayload(
        min_nodes=min_nodes,
        total=len(dups),
        exact_total=sum(1 for g in dups if g.exact),
        variant_total=len(variants),
        near_total=len(near),
        shown=min(top_n, len(dups)),
        duplicated_functions=sum(g.member_count for g in dups),
        duplicates=_shape(dups),
        variants=_shape(variants),
        near_miss=_shape(near),
        note=note,
    )


def _empty_subgraph(graph):
    import networkx as nx

    empty: nx.DiGraph = nx.DiGraph()
    empty.graph["root"] = graph.graph.get("root")
    empty.graph["parse_errors"] = graph.graph.get("parse_errors", ())
    return empty


def _graph_payload_from(
    graph,
    *,
    unresolved: tuple[str, ...] = (),
    unresolved_hints: tuple[UnresolvedHint, ...] = (),
) -> GraphPayload:
    data = graph_to_dict(graph)
    nodes = tuple(
        GraphNode(
            id=n["id"],
            external=bool(n.get("external", False)),
            path=n.get("path"),
            is_package=n.get("is_package"),
            instability=n.get("instability"),
            propagation_cost=n.get("propagation_cost"),
            edit_risk=n.get("edit_risk"),
        )
        for n in data["nodes"]
    )
    edges = tuple(
        GraphEdge(
            source=e["source"],
            target=e["target"],
            is_relative=bool(e.get("is_relative", False)),
            lines=tuple(e.get("lines", ())),
        )
        for e in data["edges"]
    )
    return GraphPayload(
        root=data["root"],
        parse_errors=tuple(data["parse_errors"]),
        nodes=nodes,
        edges=edges,
        unresolved=unresolved,
        unresolved_hints=unresolved_hints,
    )


def _refactor_note(
    *,
    lens: str,
    rows: list,
    git_available: bool,
    path: Path,
    min_risk: float,
    no_commits: bool = False,
    empty_window: bool = False,
    since: str | None = None,
) -> str | None:
    """Lens-aware empty/degraded note for archy_what_to_refactor_next.

    behavioral needs git; structural never does; fused runs both and degrades
    to structural-only off git. A non-empty single-lens result needs no note.
    An empty --since window is named so it is not mistaken for a calm codebase.
    """
    missing_git = (
        f"{path} has no commit history yet"
        if no_commits
        else f"{path} is not inside a git repository (or git is unavailable)"
    )
    if rows:
        if lens == "fused" and not git_available:
            return (
                f"{missing_git}; "
                "the CC x churn behavioral lens was skipped and this ranking is "
                "structural-only (edit-risk). Run inside git for the fused view."
            )
        return None
    if empty_window and since and git_available:
        return (
            f"No commits in the --since window ({since}). "
            "Widen the window or omit --since to use full history."
        )
    if lens == "behavioral":
        if not git_available:
            return (
                f"{missing_git}; "
                "the behavioral lens needs git history to compute per-file churn. "
                "Use lens='structural' for a git-free 'is this edit dangerous?' "
                "signal instead."
            )
        return (
            "No behavioral hotspots surfaced: no file is both complex and "
            "frequently changed (CC x churn). The project is likely small, "
            "young, or structurally clean."
        )
    if lens == "structural":
        return (
            f"No module is central and fragile above min_risk={min_risk}. Lower "
            "min_risk (pass 0 to surface every module) to widen the lens."
        )
    # fused: the only lens left once behavioral and structural have returned
    if git_available:
        return (
            "No refactoring priorities surfaced: no file is both complex and "
            "frequently changed (CC x churn hotspots: 0), and no module is "
            f"central and fragile above min_risk={min_risk} (0). The project is "
            "likely small, young, or structurally clean - there is genuinely "
            "nothing to prioritize right now. Lower min_risk to widen the "
            "structural lens."
        )
    return (
        f"{missing_git}, so the "
        "CC x churn behavioral lens was skipped and only the structural "
        f"edit-risk lens ran. No module is central and fragile above "
        f"min_risk={min_risk}, so nothing was surfaced. Lower min_risk to widen "
        "the structural lens."
    )


def run_what_to_refactor_next(
    path: Path, *, lens: str = "fused", top_n: int, since: str | None, min_risk: float
) -> WhatToRefactorPayload:
    _validate_refactor_lens(lens)
    if top_n <= 0:
        raise ValueError(f"top_n must be >= 1; got {top_n}")
    if not 0.0 <= min_risk <= 1.0:
        raise ValueError(f"min_risk must be in [0, 1]; got {min_risk}")
    # Refuse a garbage `since` even when lens='structural' skips the git call,
    # so a typo cannot silently look like "nothing to prioritize".
    if since is not None:
        repo = resolve_repo_root(path)
        if repo is not None:
            resolve_since_log_args(repo, since)

    graph = _load_graph(path, internal_only=True)
    # The behavioral lens needs git; the structural lens never does, so skip the
    # git call entirely for structural (since is irrelevant there). A repo with
    # zero commits degrades the same way but gets its own note wording.
    no_commits = False
    if lens == "structural":
        churn = None
    else:
        try:
            churn = git_churn(path, since=since)
        except NoCommitsError:
            churn = None
            no_commits = True
    git_available = churn is not None

    rows = compute_refactor_priorities(graph, churn=churn, min_risk=min_risk)
    if lens == "behavioral":
        # Keep only rows the behavioral lens fired on and restore the pure
        # CC x churn ranking (the fused `priority` would let a both-lens module
        # outrank a bigger pure hotspot).

def test_archy_impact_rejects_max_chains_zero(acyclic_project: Path):
    """MCP archy_impact must reject max_chains=0 the way the CLI does (#640).

    CLI `impact --max-chains 0` raises ClickException with a fixed message.
    Without the matching MCP guard, max_chains=0 silently returns impacted
    modules with empty chains (chains_omitted > 0) and no refusal.
    """
    from archy.mcp_compat import ToolError

    server = create_server()
    path = str(acyclic_project)
    message = "--max-chains must be negative (for all) or positive (for a limit); got 0"
    with pytest.raises(ValueError) as caught:
        run_impact(acyclic_project, files=[Path("pkg/b.py")], max_chains=0)
    assert str(caught.value) == message
    # mcp 2.x wraps as ToolError("Error executing tool <name>: <msg>"); pin the
    # refusal reaches the agent, not the exact outer wording.
    with pytest.raises(ToolError):
        _call_tool(
            server,
            "archy_impact",
            {"path": path, "files": ["pkg/b.py"], "max_chains": 0},
        )

def test_archy_dsm_rejects_an_unknown_group_by_or_weight_before_scanning(
    acyclic_project: Path, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch, kwargs: dict[str, str], name: str
):
    """group_by/weight used to be cast() straight into build_dsm, so an invalid
    value was only caught once the DSM pydantic model was built, after a full
    scan (#645). A scan that never runs cannot raise, so a `_load_graph` that
    fails if called pins "validated up front" directly.
    """

    def boom(*args, **kwargs):
        raise AssertionError(f"{name} must be validated before the project is scanned")

    monkeypatch.setattr("archy.mcp_runs._load_graph", boom)

    # Kept str-only (group_by/weight/response_format) so `**base` unifies to
    # `dict[str, str]`; mixing in the None/int fields below would widen that
    # to `str | None | int` and break every str-typed param at the call site.
    base: dict[str, str] = dict(
        response_format="summary",
        group_by="community",
        weight="imports",
    )
    base.update(kwargs)
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        run_dsm(
            acyclic_project,
    [
        (ContractsPayload(available=True, error="boom"), False, "boom"),
        (ContractsPayload(available=True, verified=True, unverifiable=0), True, None),
        (ContractsPayload(available=True, verified=False, unverifiable=2), False, "2 contract(s)"),
    ],
)
def test_brief_reads_the_contracts_verdict(
    tmp_path: Path, monkeypatch, contracts: ContractsPayload, checked: bool, reason_has
):
    monkeypatch.setattr("archy.mcp_runs.run_contracts", lambda *a, **k: contracts)
    project = _write_brief_project(tmp_path, with_config=True)
    payload = run_brief(project, top_n=8, with_contracts=True, include_tests=False)
    assert payload.transitive_checked is checked
    if reason_has is None:
        assert payload.transitive_unverified_reason is None
    else:
        assert reason_has in (payload.transitive_unverified_reason or "")

    summary = _dsm(tmp_path, group_by="topological")
    assert summary.back_edge_count >= 1
    assert summary.back_edges
    src, tgt = summary.back_edges[0]
    assert {src, tgt} == {"pkg.a", "pkg.b"}


def test_dsm_full_oversized_returns_too_large(tmp_path: Path, monkeypatch):
    # The full matrix is capped; over the ceiling it refuses with an explicit
    # indicator pointing at the summary / focus / package escape hatches.
    monkeypatch.setattr("archy.mcp_runs.DEFAULT_MAX_DSM_CELLS", 2)
    project = _fan_out_project(tmp_path, fan=5)  # 5 cells > cap of 2
    result = _dsm(project, response_format="full")
    assert isinstance(result, DSMTooLargePayload)
    assert result.cell_count == 5
    assert result.max_cells == 2

        runs._MANAGERS.clear()
    for manager in managers:
        manager.stop()

- **Constructor Over-Injection**: `constructor_max_arguments = 5`.
- **Number of Functions in a Single Module**: seen on #922 candidates and mcp_runs; the file-level cousin of Low Cohesion (#923) and of the 600 line warning.

def run_brief(path: Path, *, top_n: int, with_contracts: bool, include_tests: bool) -> BriefPayload:
    """Compose conventions, coverage and (optionally) contracts, as `archy brief` does."""
    if top_n < 1:
        raise ValueError(f"top_n must be >= 1; got {top_n}")
    report = compute_conventions(path, **graph_kwargs(path), include_tests=include_tests)

    coverage: LayerCoverage | None = None
    config = None
    config_path = discover_config(path)
    if config_path is not None:
        try:
            config = load_config(config_path)
            coverage = compute_coverage(_build_graph(path, **scan_kwargs(config)), config)
        except LayerConfigError:
            # A malformed archy.yaml is `archy_check`'s to report. Here it would
            # replace the whole briefing with one error.
            config = coverage = None

    contracts = run_contracts(path, config_filename=None) if with_contracts else None
    checked, unverifiable_reason = (
        contracts_verdict(contracts) if contracts is not None else (False, None)
    )

    reason: str | None = None
    if config is not None and coverage is not None and not checked:
        if unverifiable_reason:
            reason = unverifiable_reason
        elif contracts_unverified(config, coverage, []):
            n = len(config.forbid)
            stem = f"{n} forbid {'rule' if n == 1 else 'rules'} declared"
            if contracts is not None:
                reason = (
                    f"{stem} and still unverified: archy_brief(contracts=True) "
                    f"produced no transitive verdict ({contracts.error})."
                )
            else:
                reason = (
                    f"{stem}, but this brief runs no direct-edge check and the layers "
                    "govern too little of the graph to verify them; "
                    "archy_brief(contracts=True) evaluates them transitively via import-linter."
                )

    return BriefPayload(
        conventions=_bound_conventions(report, top_n),
        coverage=coverage,
        contracts=contracts,
        transitive_checked=checked,
        transitive_unverified_reason=reason,
    )


def _bound_conventions(report: ConventionsReport, top_n: int) -> BriefConventions:
    """Truncate the ranked sections to `top_n`, recording the untruncated totals."""
    fields = {name: getattr(report, name) for name in ConventionsReport.model_fields}
    fields.update(
        naming=report.naming[:top_n],
        surfaces=report.surfaces[:top_n],
        bases=report.bases[:top_n],
        registries=tuple(
            r.model_copy(update={"literal_names": r.literal_names[:6]})
            for r in report.registries[:top_n]
        ),
    )
    return BriefConventions(
        **fields,
        top_n=top_n,
        totals={
            "naming": len(report.naming),
            "surfaces": len(report.surfaces),
            "gates": len(report.gates),
            "errors": len(report.errors),
            "bases": len(report.bases),
            "registries": len(report.registries),
            "export_gaps": len(report.export_gaps),
            "doc_gaps": len(report.doc_gaps),
        },
    )


def run_score(
    path: Path,
    *,
    internal_only: bool,
    record: bool,
    strict: bool,
    strict_tolerance: float,
) -> ScorePayload:
    if not 0.0 <= strict_tolerance <= 1.0:
        raise ValueError(f"strict_tolerance must be in [0, 1]; got {strict_tolerance}")

    graph = _load_graph(path, internal_only=internal_only)
    score = compute_score(graph)
    if score.inputs.module_count == 0 and (record or strict):
        raise ValueError(
            f"{zero_modules_reason(path, 'scored')}; refusing to "
            f"{'record' if record else 'gate against history'}"
        )
    history_path = path / ".archy" / "history.jsonl"

    gate: ScoreGate | None = None
    if strict:
        rows = read_history(history_path)
        if rows:
            previous = rows[-1]
            delta = score.overall - previous.overall
            gate = ScoreGate(
                previous=previous.overall,
                previous_commit=previous.commit,
                previous_timestamp=previous.timestamp,
                current=score.overall,
                delta=delta,
                tolerance=strict_tolerance,
                passed=delta >= -strict_tolerance,
            )
        else:
            gate = ScoreGate(
                previous=None,
                current=score.overall,
                delta=None,
                tolerance=strict_tolerance,
                passed=True,
            )

    if record:
        commit, branch = git_metadata(path)
        append_history(history_path, row_from_score(score, commit=commit, branch=branch))

    return ScorePayload(
        overall=score.overall,
        components=score_components(score),
        inputs=score.inputs,
        gate=gate,
    )

Option 1 matches the stated intent. Either way, the CLI renderer (`cli_render_check._brief_to_text`) and the MCP payload need to agree (#371 three-surface rule).

Add the test first: `layers: 5` project, `run_brief(...)`, assert it returns coverage `None` (option 1) or raises `ValueError`-family with the file path (option 2).

content.text:
PR #925 is merged and its branch deleted. I've stopped iterating, as you asked.

**CI.** Every GitHub Actions job was green on the final head (`02b2cff9`). That covers the test matrix on Ubuntu, macOS and Windows, mcp 2.x compatibility, `check`, `score-delta`, CodeQL and the three Analyze jobs. I merged on that basis.

**CodeScene.** I did not treat the CodeScene PR check as part of CI, and it was still red. Its remaining comments are findings carried over from the old `mcp_runs.py` plus file-level smells on the new modules. If you want that check green before merging in future, say so, because it can't go green for a module split.

**Comments on #925.** Of the 30 CodeScene comments, I fixed these:
- `_pagerank` (complexity and nesting depth).
- `_warm_or_cold` (5 arguments down to 4).
- `_refactor_note` (8 arguments down to 1, via a frozen model).
- `_validate_refactor_args` (split in two).
- The `run_brief` and `run_score` Complex Method findings, via extracted helpers (`_brief_coverage`, `_unverified_forbid_reason`, `_score_gate`).

I also fixed two stale docstrings found in review. About 20 findings remain. Several are public tool signatures with 5 to 8 parameters (`run_graph`, `run_dsm`, `run_duplicates`), which change only if the tool surface changes. That is #926's territory.

**Result.** The weighted score is 8.50 on main (8.00 at the start of this pass). The new modules score 10.00 (core), 8.54 (git), 7.96 (check) and 7.96 (graph).

**Findings from mutation testing.** I added tests for the strict score gate's tolerance boundary, the garbage `since` refusal, and the duplicates note. I also found a real bug: `archy brief` with a malformed `archy.yaml` fails outright, because the error handler written to prevent that is unreachable. That is filed as #929.

**Tickets this round:**
- #926: Missing Arguments Abstractions.
- #927: Primitive Obsession, Constructor Over-Injection and Number of Functions.
- #928: CodeScene's test checks.
- #929: the brief bug.

**Not done.** `graph.py` (6.11) and `mcp.py` (6.43) are still unsplit. The remaining Complex Method findings in `dsm`, `diff`, `duplicates` and `conventions_families` are untouched.

On 2026-11-09 the user asked for an iterative code-health pass on archy driven by the CodeScene CLI (`cs`, installed, authed; `cs review FILE --output-format json`, `cs check FILE` = lint-style lines, `cs delta main` = per-file before/after with thresholds). They also granted **merge discretion** ("merge PRs using your own discretion and judgement"); my bar: all CI checks green incl. CodeScene, no unresolved review findings in the diff, scope matches the PR. A pending macOS job was called "always delayed", but the user later said green means merge.

**Why:** the user wants archy to give feedback like CodeScene, and archy's own code to score well; CodeScene's PR bot has failed 3 of 8 PRs on NEW code after push (#865, #868, #881).

**Method that worked (per file, one PR each):** `cs check` the new helpers BEFORE pushing (my first helpers kept introducing new smells: 5 args, nesting 4); prove behaviour with a byte-for-byte output diff old vs new on a fixed corpus with `PYTHONHASHSEED=0` (use `git stash` for the old side; verify the probe captured real output, twice it captured errors); mutation-check the rewritten rules, and where tests do not guard them use a randomised differential against the old implementation loaded from `git show origin/main:...`; AST-compare changed function names against main; DeepWork review; fix review findings (it caught NamedTuple vs frozen BaseModel, DRY, unexplained local import).

**State:** scores at start / now: conventions 2.93 -> 4.76 (PR #890), cli_render 3.59 -> 5.08 (merged #876), graph 4.44 -> 6.11 (merged #883). Next lowest: cli.py 4.40, mcp_runs.py 4.60, layers.py 4.85. Mean over 48 files barely moves (8.58 -> 8.67) because most files are already 10; file-level smells need module splits (#878).

**Ticket map:** #870 research (result in bench/health_repro_results.md: Args/Large/Nest/Conditional reproduce, Complex Method 0.673; Spearman -0.889), #871 `archy health`, #872 delta gate, #873 config + suppression, #884 PR annotations (CodeScene-style inline feedback, `--format github`), #886 cyclomatic definition (cs counts `raise`, not ternary/case; archy is radon-compatible by design; cs-style recount gives 0.849), #875 PYTHONHASHSEED nondeterminism in conventions, #877 run `cs delta` pre-push, #878 module splits, #880 every module labelled "hotspot", #882 clone_or_update loses the reason, #888 26% dropped files unexplained, #889 nine of ten mutations survive in conventions helpers.

**How to apply:** do not propose adding smell axes to `archy score` (the OECD gate is recorded on #870); do not claim any smell predicts anything (vendor claim, unverified); file a ticket for every finding per [[feedback-file-tickets-progressively]]; check CodeScene feedback per [[feedback-check-codescene]].

**Decision 2026-11-09 (owner): do NOT change `archy score`'s cyclomatic count (#886).** It stays radon-compatible; no baseline resets. Only open question: whether `archy health` uses a separate CodeScene-compatible count or reports Complex Method as not reproducible (decide in #871). Never touch `archy.complexity` for this.

**TARGET (owner, 2026-11-09): keep iterating until code health is over 9.0, ideally near 10.** The metric that counts is CodeScene's LoC-weighted project average, NOT the unweighted mean of file scores: 2026-11-09 evening it was 6.95 weighted vs 8.70 unweighted over 48 `src/archy` files / 18,149 code lines. Seven files hold 81% of the gap (cli 19.6%, conventions 13.7%, cli_render 13.6%, mcp_runs 11.6%, layers 8.6%, graph 8.0%, mcp 6.0%). A file needs <=600 code lines and mean cc <4 to clear the file-level smells, so function extraction alone cannot reach 9: plan is module splits of those seven files (new modules must be added to the `layers:` lists in archy.yaml and headers regenerated) plus function work. Be honest in reports about the weighted number, never the flattering one.

def test_a_compiled_extension_wins_over_a_stub_for_the_same_module(tmp_path: Path):
    """`fast.so` beside `fast.pyi` is one module, and the binary is the file recorded."""
    from archy.graph import discover_modules

    pkg = tmp_path / "pkg"
    pkg.mkdir()
    (pkg / "__init__.py").write_text("")
    (pkg / "fast.pyi").write_text("")
    (pkg / "fast.so").write_text("")

    modules = {m.qualname: m for m in discover_modules(tmp_path)}

    assert modules["pkg.fast"].path.name == "fast.so"
    assert [m.qualname for m in modules.values()].count("pkg.fast") == 1


def test_a_soft_ignored_name_is_skipped_when_the_path_is_outside_the_scan_root(tmp_path: Path):
    """No directory can be probed for an `__init__.py` there, so the name decides (`venv`)."""
    from archy.graph import is_ignored_path

    root = tmp_path / "project"
    root.mkdir()
    outside = tmp_path / "elsewhere" / "venv" / "mod.py"

    assert is_ignored_path(outside, DEFAULT_IGNORED_DIRS, root) is True


def test_a_declared_root_that_is_not_a_directory_is_not_a_package_root(tmp_path: Path):
    pkg = tmp_path / "pkg"
    pkg.mkdir()
    (pkg / "__init__.py").write_text("")

    roots = _find_package_roots(tmp_path, DEFAULT_IGNORED_DIRS, ("no_such_dir",))

    assert roots == [pkg.resolve()]


def test_a_reexport_cycle_stops_at_the_first_repeat_not_after_a_fixed_number_of_hops():
    """a -> b -> c -> a for one name: following hops blindly for 8 steps would land on `a`."""
    from archy.graph import _follow_reexport_chains

    maps = {"a": {"X": "b"}, "b": {"X": "c"}, "c": {"X": "a"}}

    _follow_reexport_chains(maps)

    assert maps["a"]["X"] == "c"
EOF

import ast, glob, collections, json
from pathlib import Path
SRC = Path("src/archy/graph.py"); text = SRC.read_text(); lines = text.splitlines(); tree = ast.parse(text)
GROUPS = {
 "graph_models": ["_EXTENSION_SUFFIXES_BY_LENGTH","HARD_IGNORED_DIRS","SOFT_IGNORED_DIRS","DEFAULT_IGNORED_DIRS","DEFAULT_MAX_MODULES","_MAX_COLLISIONS_SHOWN","ScanTooLargeError","QualnameCollisionError","Module","effective_max_modules","UnresolvedHint"],

 "graph_assemble": ["assemble_graph","_add_module_nodes","_Resolver","_add_import_edges","_add_module_import_edges","_add_call_edges","_add_module_call_edges","_add_kind","_add_or_extend_edge","_add_or_extend_call_edge","_cc_aggregates","graph_to_dict","internal_subgraph","internal_module_count","zero_modules_reason"],
 "graph_hints": ["_SUGGEST_MIN_SIMILARITY","_SUGGEST_MARGIN","suggest_modules","hint_unresolved","_hint_for","suggest_files","_FileIndex","_file_index","_file_hint","_module_parts","_in_callers_form","resolve_modules","_path_index","_resolve_one"],
}
DOCS = {
 "graph_models": "The value objects and limits a scan shares: Module, scan-size and collision errors, ignored directories.",
 "graph_discovery": "Finding a project's Python files and naming each one: package roots, qualnames, ignore rules.",
 "graph_resolve": "Resolving imports and call targets to modules, including re-exports and aliases.",
 "graph_assemble": "Assembling the import graph from parsed modules, and reading it back out.",
 "graph_hints": "Did-you-mean hints and name resolution for a module or file the caller mistyped.",
}
def node_name(n):
    if isinstance(n,(ast.FunctionDef,ast.ClassDef)): return [n.name]
    if isinstance(n,(ast.Assign,ast.AnnAssign)):
        ts = n.targets if isinstance(n,ast.Assign) else [n.target]; return [t.id for t in ts if isinstance(t,ast.Name)]
    return []
items = [n for n in tree.body if node_name(n)]
spans = {}
for n in items:
    start = min([d.lineno for d in getattr(n,"decorator_list",[])]+[n.lineno]); s = start
    while s-2 >= 0 and lines[s-2].lstrip().startswith("#"): s -= 1
    spans[node_name(n)[0]] = (s, n.end_lineno)
assigned = {x for g in GROUPS.values() for x in g}
extra = [x for x in assigned if x not in spans]; assert not extra, extra
remaining = [node_name(n)[0] for n in items if node_name(n)[0] not in assigned]
print("stays in graph.py:", remaining)
first = min(v[0] for v in spans.values()); doc_end = tree.body[0].end_lineno
header = "\n".join(lines[doc_end:first-1]).strip("\n")
orig_doc = text.split('"""')[1]
def body(members): return "\n\n\n".join("\n".join(lines[spans[m][0]-1:spans[m][1]]) for m in sorted(members, key=lambda m: spans[m][0]))
for name, members in GROUPS.items():
    Path(f"src/archy/{name}.py").write_text(f'"""{DOCS[name]}"""\n\n{header}\n\n\n{body(members)}\n')
owner = {n: m for m, ns in GROUPS.items() for n in ns}
for n in remaining: owner[n] = "graph"
imported = set()
for p in glob.glob("src/**/*.py", recursive=True)+glob.glob("tests/**/*.py", recursive=True)+glob.glob("bench/**/*.py", recursive=True):
    if p.endswith("src/archy/graph.py"): continue
    try: t = ast.parse(open(p).read())
    except Exception: continue
    for n in ast.walk(t):
        if isinstance(n, ast.ImportFrom) and n.module == "archy.graph": imported |= {a.name for a in n.names}
unknown = imported - set(owner); assert not unknown, unknown
reexp = sorted(n for n in imported if owner[n] != "graph")
by_mod = collections.defaultdict(list)
for nm in reexp: by_mod[owner[nm]].append(nm)
imports = "".join(f"from archy.{m} import {', '.join(ns)}\n" for m, ns in sorted(by_mod.items()))
allnames = ",\n".join(f'    "{n}"' for n in sorted(imported))
SRC.write_text(f'"""{orig_doc}"""\n\n{header}\n{imports}\n\n{body(remaining)}\n\n__all__ = [\n{allnames},\n]\n')
new_text = "".join(Path(f"src/archy/{n}.py").read_text() for n in [*GROUPS, "graph"])
new_lines = set(l.strip() for l in new_text.splitlines())
body_lines = [l.strip() for l in lines[doc_end:] if l.strip()]
lost = [l for l in body_lines if l not in new_lines and not l.startswith(("import ","from "))]
print("re-exports", len(reexp), "| original body lines:", len(body_lines), "| lost:", len(lost)); print("\n".join(lost[:10]))
json.dump({**GROUPS, "graph": remaining}, open("/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-hosanglee-archy/2baa2158-73fd-4a98-bed1-d7f35235506f/scratchpad/groups_graph.json","w"))
